meta.headline: Does a heat pump cut carbon emissions on today's grid, even where power comes from coal?
meta.seoTitle: Do heat pumps cut carbon emissions on today's grid?

dek.text: Most of the studies here find that replacing gas heating with a heat pump cuts a home's carbon emissions, by 36 percent in measured British homes on today's grid; where coal powers the grid the gain can vanish, and how many homes that affects is not settled.

assertions.text: In today's terms, British households that replaced a gas boiler with a heat pump cut the CO2eq footprint of their energy use by 36%.
qualifications: The dek names the British measurement, the coal exception and the unsettled count in the same sentence.

assertions.text: RMI found the short-term impact of electrification increases carbon emissions in Chicago, whose grid has coal as its marginal generator most of the year.

description.text: British homes cut energy emissions 36% after swapping gas for a heat pump; on coal-heavy grids the gain can vanish, and how often is not settled.

assertions.text: In today's terms, British households that replaced a gas boiler with a heat pump cut the CO2eq footprint of their energy use by 36%.
qualifications: The description names the coal exception and says how often it applies is not settled.

assertions.text: RMI found the short-term impact of electrification increases carbon emissions in Chicago, whose grid has coal as its marginal generator most of the year.

sections.name: hook
sections.heading: Is a heat pump cleaner when the power plant burns gas or coal?

sentences.text: A heat pump burns nothing inside the house, but the power station that feeds it may burn gas or coal, so does trading a gas furnace or boiler for one actually lower a home's carbon emissions?
This article sets out the evidence study by study, with the grid and the years each result assumes, because those are what decide the answer.

sections.name: setup
sections.heading: Who says heat pumps are cleaner, and who doubts it

sentences.text: Sceptics point at the power plants: a letter in the Boston Globe objected that "the majority of electricity in Massachusetts is sourced from gas- and coal-fired power plants", and the American Gas Association contends that a household heating with gas can have a lower carbon footprint than one with a heat pump.

assertions.text: A letter to the Boston Globe warned that most Massachusetts electricity comes from gas- and coal-fired plants, and the American Gas Association argues that a natural gas home can have a lower carbon footprint than a heat pump home.

quote.text: the majority of electricity in Massachusetts is sourced from gas- and coal-fired power plants
quote.speaker: Boston Globe

sentences.text: On the other side, the channel Technology Connections argues that efficiency wins even when the electricity comes from a gas-fired power plant, because "a heat pump can move more heat energy into a living space than the natural gas itself contains".

assertions.text: Technology Connections argues that even with a natural gas fired power plant, a heat pump can move more heat into a home than the gas itself contains.

quote.text: a heat pump can move more heat energy into a living space than the natural gas itself contains
quote.speaker: Technology Connections

sections.name: investigation
sections.heading: What the studies measured and what they modelled

sentences.text: The most direct evidence comes from British households that swapped a gas boiler for a heat pump: a working paper published by the National Bureau of Economic Research converted the change in their energy use into emissions, and in today's terms found a saving of 1.16 tonnes a year of CO2 equivalent for each household, or 36 percent of what their energy use emitted before the switch.

assertions.text: In today's terms, replacing a gas boiler with a heat pump is equivalent to a 1.16 tonne reduction in CO2eq emissions per household per year, a 36% reduction on the households' pre-heat-pump CO2eq footprint from annual energy consumption.

sentences.text: Assuming the grid keeps decarbonizing over a 20-year working life, the same authors put the saving across the heat pump's lifespan at 68 percent; that figure is a projection, and the saving above is the one for today's grid.

assertions.text: Assuming a 20-year heat pump lifespan and an electricity grid that decarbonizes, the authors estimate heat pumps can reduce a household's CO2 equivalent emissions by 68% throughout their operational lifespan.
qualifications: s06 itself says the 68 percent is a lifetime projection on a cleaner grid, not today's figure.

sentences.text: A Fraunhofer ISE study of heat pumps in existing buildings, counting the German electricity mix quarter by quarter, found that in 2024 the heat pumps it examined emitted on average 64 percent less CO2 than gas heating systems.

assertions.text: Using quarterly calculated emission values from the German electricity mix, the CO2 emissions of the examined heat pumps were in 2024 on average 64 percent lower than those of gas heating systems.
qualifications: s07 names the grid (German), the year (2024) and the sample (the heat pumps the study examined).

sentences.text: The Canadian Climate Institute, drawing on the International Energy Agency and a consultancy rather than on measurements of its own, puts the cut at between 20 and 30 percent against gas furnaces even where the electricity is relatively emissions-intensive.

assertions.text: Citing the International Energy Agency (2022) and a consultancy (2021), the Canadian Climate Institute says that even on relatively emissions-intensive electricity, heat pumps emit between 20 and 30 per cent less carbon than gas furnaces because of their high efficiency.
qualifications: s08 says the range is drawn from other work, not measured on a named grid.

blocks.caption: Cut in carbon emissions from replacing gas heating with a heat pump, by study; the baselines differ: NBER measures the whole home's energy footprint, Fraunhofer ISE and the Canadian Climate Institute the heating against gas

rows.label: UK households replacing a gas boiler, today's grid, whole-home footprint (NBER working paper)
UK households replacing a gas boiler, projected over the heat pump's life on a decarbonizing grid, whole-home footprint (NBER working paper)
Heat pumps examined in existing German buildings, German grid counted quarterly (Fraunhofer ISE)
Heat pumps against gas furnaces on relatively emissions-intensive electricity, cited from other studies (Canadian Climate Institute)

sentences.text: RMI's analysis of electrifying buildings tested the coal objection directly, comparing electric heating with natural gas on the grid of its day, and found it reduced carbon in Oakland, Houston and Providence.

assertions.text: RMI found that electrifying space and water heating reduced carbon compared with natural gas on the electric grid of the time in Oakland, Houston and Providence.
qualifications: The callout after s09 gives Chicago, where electrification raised emissions in the short term.

sentences.text: Chicago went the other way: because coal was the generator answering extra demand there for most of the year, the short-term effect of electrifying heat was higher carbon emissions, though RMI expected that to swing in favour of electrification, in Chicago and nationally, as coal plants retire.

assertions.text: Because the grid serving Chicago has coal as its marginal generator most of the year, RMI found the short-term impact of electrification there increases carbon emissions.
qualifications: s10 states the Chicago exception in full, as a short-term result.

assertions.text: RMI expects the long-term impact to swing in favor of electrification in Chicago and nationally with continued retirement of coal plants.
qualifications: s10 words the swing as RMI's expectation, not a result.

sentences.text: How common is Chicago's case across the United States? A national model of US houses found that adopting a heat pump raises CO2 emissions in only 2.1 percent of the housing stock, about 1.7 million houses, counted across all houses rather than gas-heated ones, and the estimate assumes grid CO2 emissions fall by 45 percent over a 15-year heat pump life.

assertions.text: Deetjen et al. estimate heat pump adoption increases CO2 emissions in only 1.7 million houses, 2.1% of the US housing stock, based on historical grid operations and the assumption that over the heat pump's 15 years life electric grid CO2 emissions decrease by 45%.
qualifications: s11 carries the 45 percent grid-cleaning assumption beside the 2.1 percent and says the share is of all houses.

blocks.caption: A US national model: the share of houses where a heat pump raises emissions, shown with the grid assumption and equipment life behind it.

sentences.text: Researchers at NREL and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory modelled every home adopting an air-source heat pump at once, whatever it heated with before, and found average greenhouse gas savings positive in every state under every heat pump and future grid scenario they ran, including the conservative high renewable energy cost scenario.

assertions.text: Wilson et al. model full, immediate ASHP adoption and find average annual GHG savings are positive in every state and in every heat pump and future grid scenario, even the conservative high renewable energy cost grid scenario.
qualifications: s12 says the scenarios are future grids and the homes are not gas-heated ones alone; s13 adds that these are state averages.

sentences.text: Those are state averages on grids projected forward, so they say nothing about how many individual homes come out behind on today's grid.

assertions.text: Wilson et al. report average annual GHG savings per household by state under different future grid scenarios.

sentences.text: A Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory study of home retrofits shows the grid's weight from the other side: its electrification projects with solar panels sat mostly in states with low-carbon electricity, where fuel switching sharply boosted carbon reductions.

assertions.text: In LBNL's retrofit study, projects in the Electrification with PV cluster tended to be located in states with low carbon intensity of grid electricity, and fuel switching dramatically boosted carbon reductions in that cluster.
qualifications: s14 says the projects included solar panels and sat in low-carbon states; s15 gives the authors' expectation for dirtier grids.

sentences.text: Its authors expect similar projects to save less carbon in states whose electricity is more carbon-intensive, so those results do not carry over to a coal-heavy grid.

assertions.text: LBNL's authors expect similar electrification projects to have lower carbon savings in states with higher carbon intensity in their electricity.
qualifications: s15 is the authors' expectation, worded as one.

sections.name: answer
sections.heading: So does a heat pump cut emissions on today's grid?

sentences.text: On most grids the studies here say yes: the British saving above was measured against today's grid, and RMI found that electrification already cut carbon compared with natural gas in all but the most coal-heavy systems, as those systems stood when it wrote.

assertions.text: In today's terms, British households that replaced a gas boiler with a heat pump reduced the CO2eq emissions of their energy use.
RMI states that electrification already reduces carbon with today's electric grid in all but the most coal-heavy systems, compared with natural gas as well as oil and propane.
qualifications: s16 says RMI's grid was the grid when it wrote; the callout on Chicago gives the exception.

sentences.text: What the evidence cannot yet say is how many homes on today's grid come out behind: the national US model assumes a grid that gets cleaner, the national laboratories' study projects future grids, and the coal exception rests on RMI's reading of the grid as it stood then, so the answer is well supported on most grids but not settled for all of them.

assertions.text: Deetjen et al. base their estimate on the assumption that electric grid CO2 emissions decrease over the heat pump's life.
Wilson et al. estimate savings under future grid scenarios.
RMI found the short-term impact of electrification increases carbon emissions in Chicago, whose grid has coal as its marginal generator most of the year.

sentences.text: Why the studies differ is not something this evidence settles, and they measure against different baselines; RMI and the British study do tie their results to the grid: RMI links its Chicago exception to coal answering extra demand, and the British saving grows in the projection that has the grid decarbonizing.

assertions.text: RMI attributes the short-term increase in Chicago to coal being the marginal generator on its grid most of the year.
Emissions savings rise over the heat pump's lifespan as the electricity grid decarbonizes.

sections.name: takeaway
sections.heading: What to ask before counting on the carbon saving

sentences.text: If cutting carbon is your reason for switching, ask your electricity supplier which plants run when winter demand rises, and whether coal is still among them.
The answer tells you which of the results above describes your home, and whether it is likely to change while your heat pump is still running.
